transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess... I called the employee assistance program at work. They suggested I come in. It's mostly my sleep, I think. I just... I lie awake a lot, going over things from the office, or stuff at home. Then I wake up around 3 or 4 in the morning and can't get back to sleep. I just feel like I'm not really resting.
Are these sleep issues affecting your daily life or work in any way?

I mean... I'm still showing up to work. Just... things slip a little, I guess. My forecasts, or prep for clients. The team has had to cover a few gaps for me lately. And at home... I don't know, I'm probably just less present with my wife and the kids than I used to be. But... yeah. That's about it.
Do you feel anxious or worried during the day?
Not really. I mean, I guess I get a little stressed about work sometimes, but... no, I wouldn't say I'm anxious. Just tired.
Do you have any disturbing dreams or nightmares?
No... not really. I don't think I dream much at all, to be honest. Or I just don't remember them. So, no.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about everyday things?
No, not really. Like I said... I just feel tired. I don't really worry about much.
How long have you been having these sleep problems?

Probably about a year and two months, I guess. It, uh... it started around the time things got bad at home. The arguments, I mean. They started getting a lot worse back then, so... yeah. A little over a year.
Do you find that you're sleeping at the same times every day, or has your sleep schedule changed over the past year?

Yeah, it's changed. I'm barely sleeping right anymore. I just... I lie in bed, mostly just replaying work, or the arguments at home. And then I end up waking up around 3 or 4. 

I just start every day feeling like I never really rested. It's, uh... it's actually what finally made me call the employee assistance program.
Do you have trouble sleeping when you want to, but find yourself feeling more alert at the same times every day?
Not really, no. I don't... I don't think there's a time of day where I feel alert. I'm just mostly tired.
Do you find yourself feeling tired at the same times every day?
Um... no, not really. I don't think there's a specific time. I just... I kind of feel tired all day. It doesn't really change.
Do you think your sleep problems might be related to your body's internal clock?
I don't really know. Um... I haven't thought about it like that. I just... I just know I'm not sleeping well.
Do you think your body has a regular sleep-wake cycle?
I'm not sure... I haven't really noticed if it does. Um... probably not, but I couldn't really say for sure.
Do you often find yourself feeling most awake and alert late at night?
Um... no, not really. I wouldn't say I ever really feel alert right now. Even late at night, I'm just... still tired.
Do you think your sleep issues would improve if you could establish a consistent sleep schedule?
I mean... maybe. I haven't really tried it. Um... it's hard to say if it would actually make a difference.
Do you think your sleep problems might be caused by your body having a hard time following a normal day-night cycle?
I don't know... I haven't really thought about it like that. Um... I just know I'm tired. I couldn't really tell you if it's my cycle or... something else.
Do you think your sleep problems would improve if you were able to go to bed and wake up at the same times every day?
I'm not really sure. Um... I guess it's possible. But I don't really know if it would actually change much. I just... haven't tried.
Do you think your sleep issues are related to the time of day you sleep, rather than the amount of sleep you get?
I haven't really paid attention to that. Um... I just sleep when I can, I guess. I don't really know if the time on the clock matters more than the actual hours.
Have you ever experienced a period of at least several days where you felt like you were sleeping at a time that was out of sync with the rest of the world?
I don't really know... I mean, I'm just asleep when I'm asleep. I haven't really noticed if it's out of sync with everyone else. I just... sleep when I can.
Have you ever found yourself regularly sleeping during the day and being awake at night for an extended period?
No, I don't think so. Um... I mean, I might be up late sometimes, but I don't sleep all day. It's mostly just... normal hours, I guess. So, no.
Do you usually go to bed later than most people and wake up later than you need to?
Um, no, not really. I go to bed at a normal time, I think. And I get up when my alarm goes off for work, so... no. I don't really do that.
Have you ever experienced a period where you felt like your sleep pattern repeated every 25 hours or more, rather than the usual 24 hours?
No... I don't really know how I would even notice something like that. My days are just regular days. So, no.
